one_star_reviews.text:
Stayed here for one night and would not stay again.

The positives are the beautiful views and the good restaurant downstairs.

Unfortunately, the apartment needs a thorough clean and some updating. The sofa was heavily stained and very uncomfortable, the shower flooded the bathroom despite being careful, and no shower mat was provided. The towels were still slightly damp when we arrived and needed to be hung up to finish drying.

The outdoor wooden benches were also old and covered in a sticky, sap-like residue. Even the TV is mounted in such an awkward position that it’s difficult to watch comfortably.

The beautiful views are the main saving grace, but overall I wouldn’t recommend staying here.

one_star_reviews.text:
Wow... Half of Spain is getting up to deceive the other half. I went to an event nearby and stopped by this shop for a box of Boroñinas (a type of Spanish pastry), and I got ripped off. Before buying them, after asking the price, I asked if I could have a box to check the ingredients and net weight. I saw that the NET weight was 300 grams and that it didn't contain any ingredients that I thought were unnecessary, so I asked for a box.
Knowing what's going on in this society, and out of a sense of caution, I weighed the box before eating any of them.
I've included photos; as you can see, it was 267 grams, and that's before deducting the weight of the box.
I called the shop and asked if there shouldn't be 300 grams of Boroñinas in the box, and the woman who answered—who makes them and served me at the shop—told me "approximately"; that the weight is approximate and that they're counted, so there should be 12 (and yes, she gave me 12). He told me as if it weren't illegal.

They charged me €8.50 for the box. Net weight is net weight, not gross or "approximate," and putting a net weight of 300g and giving out whatever you feel like is deceiving people, period. And I hope they do the same to you wherever you go.

When I finished the product, I weighed the box again, and it's 35g, so out of 300g net of product, 232g remain (267 - 35), a not insignificant 22%, which goes from €8.50 to over €1.80. Well, I hope you get your money's worth from the €1.50 you ripped me off for.

And it doesn't end there. In one of the Boroñinas, there was a curious piece of hazelnut shell that I bit into, and who knows how much it hurt.

I'm including photos of the full box, the scale with a calibrated weight to ensure it weighed correctly, the empty box, and the piece of shell.

one_star_reviews.text:
A terrible experience. I took my car there because I'd had several punctures repaired, and when I picked it up, it was clearly pulling to the right. I specifically asked the mechanic if they had checked the tire pressures, and he assured me they had.

Since the car was still pulling, I ended up paying another €50 for an alignment. Afterward, I checked the pressures myself, and they were completely uneven between the tires. I went to a gas station, properly adjusted the air pressure in all four tires, and, coincidentally, the car started driving fine.

The bare minimum after working on several tires is to check all four pressures before returning the vehicle. It takes two minutes, and besides, in my case, I specifically asked about it, and they told me it had been checked when it clearly hadn't.

I find it incredibly unprofessional that they returned the car to me in that condition and that I ended up paying an additional €50 for an alignment when they hadn't even checked something as basic as the tire pressures. I won't be back.

one_star_reviews.text:
The most disappointing fine dining experience I have ever had. The service was abismal from the word go. Unfriendly, cold and disinterested to the point of rudeness. I have dined in plenty of one, two and three Michelin star restaurants in my life and this is single-handedly the W O R S T one period. The atmosphere was stuffy, the room is quite bare (ok I know that’s a vibe some people like), the room was so quiet you had to whisper and it made for an uncomfortable dinner atmosphere. No music. Uncomfortable chairs. I asked if they had a drink with low sugar (I’ve been recently diagnosed with diabetes) and while in my travels this year in France and Spain, I have not had an issue finding something to drink that is not Coke Zero, which after having to ask the staff twice, was the only offer I got. I cannot believe that having a non-alcoholic pairing on the menu, they couldn’t have anything to offer. Then the food started arriving: plain, flavourless, greatly under-seasoned and with no starch or texture whatsoever. Three what seemed poached fish dishes in a row with mystery foams with little or no explanation. The wine pairing for the table was super poor: no flavour notes just a rushed mention of grape and region. no sommelier in sight, just a waiter reciting a badly written script, an 8 course tasting menu came with only 4 wines, including a heavy red wine with a fish course 😳. Water, which we paid for, was topped sporadically and since the bottle was not left at the table, we couldn’t even top ourselves! The tomato dish was the only good thing in the menu. The ice-cream element in the dessert was also nice. Took me getting up to get the bill and 10 minutes later still waiting for a waiter to bring the card machine, I had to get up again for someone to come over and take payment. How on earth do they have a Michelin star is beyond me. DO NOT WASTE your cash on this. They rely on the location and tourist, I doubt they get any repeat customer. Final bill for 4 (one vegan) on tasting menu, tree wine pairings and water for me, came to €622.00 what a waste.

I chose this restaurant because of a review and was really looking forward to trying it. Unfortunately, the experience started very poorly.

When I arrived, I waited politely for someone from the staff to notice me, but I felt like I was being ignored. Eventually, I called out and asked if there was a table available. They asked how many people, and when I said I was alone, they immediately replied that there was probably no space.

That was quite confusing — would there have been space if I had said there were two or more people? It simply made no sense.

I continued waiting and was still ignored until I asked again, at which point I was told there was no space.

I found the whole situation extremely rude and unwelcoming. Even if there genuinely was no table available, the staff could have simply acknowledged me and explained the situation politely instead of leaving me standing there feeling ignored. Very disappointing.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with this salon has been quite disappointing.

First, I booked a pedicure appointment before going on a trip, and at the last minute, they canceled it. Despite this, I decided to give them a second chance when I returned from my vacation and booked another appointment.

On the day of the appointment, I arrived at the salon at the agreed-upon time, and to my surprise, the place was closed. I tried contacting them by phone several times, without getting an answer. I even called the Santiago location to try to find out if they could inform me about what had happened, but they didn't answer either.

What I find particularly unprofessional is that no one bothered to cancel the appointment or at least notify me in advance that the salon was going to be closed. They made me travel all the way there for absolutely nothing.

Furthermore, the salon has no way of knowing if a person lives nearby, if they had to drive, take a bus, or make any other effort to get there. I believe that, at the very least, there should be responsibility and respect for customers' time.

After giving them a second chance following an initial cancellation, this situation is even more disappointing. A very unprofessional experience, and I certainly won't be booking with them again.

⚠️ Make sure to check your receipt before leaving the store!
Unfortunately, I only noticed afterwards that I had been charged for one extra bottle of sangria at the Duty Free shop at Alicante Airport. I bought 4 bottles, but 5 were charged on my receipt.
I immediately tried to contact customer service and submitted a complaint, including photos of the receipt and the 4 bottles I actually purchased. However, I still haven't received any response after two weeks.
Mistakes can happen, but I believe a customer complaint should at least be acknowledged and addressed.
That's why I would advise everyone shopping at the Duty Free shop at Alicante Airport to carefully check your receipt and the number of items before leaving, as resolving an issue afterwards does not seem to be easy.
I was charged for a product I never purchased, and after two weeks, I am still waiting for a response.

one_star_reviews.text: I'm giving it one star because I can't give it less... I took a garment in for alterations and explained to the woman in detail what I wanted. She said she could do it, and I agreed to everything. I paid and left, but when I went back to pick it up (my fault for not checking it earlier) and wore it... she hadn't done any of the things I explained to her, and she confirmed she could do them... Just a special wash (which I didn't even ask for... It was a seam...). Awful... Total disappointment... I don't think I'd go back even if it were the only dry cleaner I know.

The review is about the quality of the furniture. It's covered in a wood-effect vinyl that's peeling off. We installed a bathroom vanity in 2022 during a complete renovation. After two and a half years, the drawers started peeling. Thanks to the decorator who did the renovation, we managed to get them replaced. But now, after another year and a half, they're starting to peel again. This is a bathroom in a house with two very careful adults who are hardly ever home. The design is nice, but the quality of the finish is terrible.

one_star_reviews.text:
My daughter, an American university student studying abroad in Madrid, was taken to HLA Moncloa after becoming ill with significant upper respiratory symptoms, including persistent fever, severe coughing and congestion. While waiting, she developed what for her was a routine nosebleed after coughing very hard.

During the emergency-room visit, a nasal balloon/packing device was inserted into her nose. She maintains that she did not consent to this procedure and did not understand what the staff were doing until the device had been inserted and inflated. It caused severe pain. She repeatedly asked—and eventually begged—for the device to be removed, but the hospital declined to remove it.

IV medications, including Valium, were also administered. She maintains that these medications were given without her informed consent or an adequate explanation beforehand.
The situation deteriorated to the point that she called her mother and me from the hospital. She was extremely ill, in severe pain and increasingly impaired by the medication she had received, making it difficult for her to advocate for herself. Communication between her and the medical staff was also extremely difficult. The situation became so stressful and chaotic that the person accompanying her and assisting with translation actually lost consciousness during the episode.

Despite her repeated requests that the nasal device be removed and our insistence by telephone that no additional medications or procedures be performed, the hospital would not remove it. She was ultimately discharged with the device still in her nose, while the other medical equipment, including her IV, was removed. The attending physician appeared visibly angry and frustrated when we insisted that the device be removed and that no further interventions be performed without her agreement.

Equally troubling was what happened with the illness that had actually caused her to seek medical attention. Although some testing was performed, in our family's view the persistent fever, severe cough, congestion and worsening respiratory symptoms were not adequately diagnosed or treated during this encounter.
We therefore sought medical care independently at another Madrid hospital. There, physicians evaluated her respiratory symptoms, performed laboratory testing and throat testing, obtained chest imaging, and administered respiratory and other treatments. She was diagnosed with acute bronchitis and prescribed treatment for the underlying illness.

We later requested Lauren's complete HLA medical record, including supporting clinical documentation. Despite follow-up requests, we received only a limited set of records rather than the broader documentation we had requested.

Based upon our family's experience, I would not recommend HLA Moncloa to an English-speaking international student requiring emergency medical care.

Our greatest concern was that the illness that caused her to seek medical attention—persistent fever, severe cough, congestion and worsening respiratory symptoms—received remarkably little meaningful evaluation during the episode. We subsequently sought care independently at another Madrid hospital, where physicians performed a respiratory examination, laboratory testing, chest imaging and respiratory treatments and diagnosed acute bronchitis.

We later requested the complete HLA medical record, including supporting clinical documentation, but received only a limited set of records despite follow-up requests.

Based upon our family's experience, I would not recommend this hospital to an English-speaking international student requiring emergency care.

one_star_reviews.text:
Absolutely Awful

I’ve been to Aquapolis before and don't remember it being this bad, but after last Friday, it will definitely be my last time. We couldn't even stick it out and had to leave early! It was just terrible from start to finish.

A few reasons why we won't be back:

1) No space and zero control: There was literally nowhere to put our towels. When we finally found a tiny spot with shade, we went on a few rides, came back, and another family had taken our place. We did manage to find another better place though.

2) Ridiculous queue times:  I knew it would be busy but not to a point to where my eldest son had to wait up to two hours for rides. It was so bad that we were basically forced to pay for the speedy pass upgrade just to make the day bearable. Even with the pass, we still had to wait, though at least it was a bit less.

3) Unfair operators: My youngest was denied entry on many rides despite actually meeting the height requirement (son's height 139cm) and having an adult right there with him.

4) Total rip-off: On top of everything else, the food and drinks are completely overpriced which sadly it  is the norm of many theme parks.

Save your money and skip it. It wasn't worth the hassle, the money, or the frustration.

one_star_reviews.text: I don't recommend them. I had solar film installed on my car three years ago, and it's already purple. However, a month ago, I asked them for a quote to install film on another car I'd bought. They gave me the price, but this time I asked about the type of film they use, since I didn't want the same thing to happen as with the other car. They told me the guy who knew was on vacation and to call back in a few days. Since then, I've called several times, supposedly because this guy is back at the shop, and every time I call, they say they don't know and give me the runaround. I absolutely don't believe that a shop that's been installing solar film for years wouldn't know what kind of film they use, the brand, the specifications, or the characteristics. The only conclusion I can draw about their refusal to tell me what film they use is that it's such poor quality that they prefer not to say and let me see for myself after it's already been installed and paid for. It's pathetic. Obviously I won't post the images here; I think it's more than fair to know what you're buying before you buy it—he who has nothing to fear has nothing to hide.

We were honestly left speechless by this experience.

The wine tasting itself was very basic, with very little explanation about the wines, the production process, the fruit, aromas, or flavours. The English spoken by the staff was quite limited, so as I speak Spanish, I asked them to explain everything to me in Spanish so that I could translate it for my boyfriend. Unfortunately, this didn't make much difference, as the explanations were still very limited.

Some cheeses were served alongside the wines, but there was no explanation about the pairings or which cheese complemented each wine.

Afterwards, we discovered several rooms displaying information and the history of the winery. Nobody told us about them, invited us to explore them, or offered us any kind of tour.

What made the experience even more disappointing was when a German couple sat next to us. We immediately noticed a significant difference in the level of attention they received. There was much more conversation, explanation, and engagement with them. The sommelier even left the wine bottles on their table so they could take pictures. Considering we had booked the same type of experience, this made us feel completely overlooked and left on the side.

As for the wines themselves, we found them quite mediocre — nothing particularly special or memorable.

Unfortunately, we would not return. There is a lot of room for improvement, particularly when it comes to English communication, customer engagement, detailed explanations of the wines and pairings, and actually showing guests around the winery.

Overall, a very disappointing experience that could have been so much better.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience with the product and, above all, with the handling of my warranty claim

In April 2026, I purchased a Victron EasySolar-II 48/3000/35-32 MPPT 250/70 GX from Techno Sun. Unfortunately, the unit did not work properly from the very beginning. The PV/MPPT function did not work, while charging from a generator was possible.

The inverter was installed by an experienced and qualified installer who had previously installed several units of this type. Therefore, from the beginning, I had no reason to suspect an installation or user error.

After troubleshooting, I returned the inverter to Techno Sun under RMA10430. I also had to pay approximately €80 for shipping the approximately 28 kg defective unit back to the seller myself.

Despite repeatedly emphasizing that the matter was urgent, I waited a very long time for responses and a solution. The entire process took approximately six months.

The inverter was installed at an off-grid property that is not connected to the electricity grid and depended on this system for its electricity supply. Due to the long delay in resolving the issue, I was left without a functioning system for approximately six months, which also resulted in damage and additional costs at the property.

After inspection, I was informed that the factory had allegedly found “overvoltage to ground” and that the MPPT, PV filter and GX had been damaged. Techno Sun therefore rejected my warranty claim and referred to the possibility of lightning or another external electrical event. They offered me a replacement, but only for an additional payment, albeit at a discounted price.

I do not agree with this conclusion. From my experience, the inverter did not function correctly from the very beginning. The system was professionally installed, and I see no reasonable basis for attributing responsibility for the failure to me.

I was particularly disappointed by the reference to possible lightning damage. Based on the circumstances and the way the system was installed, to the best of my knowledge there was no actual indication that such an event had occurred. Nevertheless, the possibility of lightning was given as a reason for rejecting the warranty claim.

I was also informed that there was no warranty sticker on the unit preventing me from opening it for inspection. During my inspection, I found visibly swollen capacitors inside the unit.

What disappointed me most was that I had to pay approximately €80 myself to return a defective product, then wait for months for a solution, and ultimately be left without a functioning product and without an accepted warranty claim or refund.

I have kept the complete documentation, including the invoice, correspondence, RMA documentation, photographs and the inspection documentation.

I am sharing my experience so that potential customers can take it into consideration before purchasing from Techno Sun, particularly regarding their responsiveness, the length of the warranty process and the way warranty claims are handled.

Based on my experience, I cannot recommend Techno Sun.

one_star_reviews.text: If you're thinking about studying baking and pastry, think twice. NOTHING is practical or informative. All the months I've been enrolled, I've only seen veterinary and English classes scheduled. Imagine studying how to knead bread dough without ever seeing a real loaf, just pictures! Or how to make a good buttercream consistency with only 4 cm photos in a book. They have a virtual campus, but you're supposed to study by reading a book and then taking a quiz, and you have to find the video yourself that roughly corresponds to the topic you're reading in the book, because even the video titles don't match. I'm truly dissatisfied.

one_star_reviews.text:
The absolute worst experience I’ve had hiring a vehicle abroad, or anywhere for that matter.

Arrived to collect the vehicle, only one operator at the desk and approximately 10 people queuing, it took approximately 1.5 hours for to collect the vehicle, the service was poor and slow.

Every customer in front of me (this is not an exaggeration) had to return to the desk due to damage to the vehicle that was not recorded on the document they had signed. With this in mind I did not have high expectations.

When I was finally served I was given a vehicle in a lower class than what I had paid for, I received a smaller vehicle than I had booked and this caused issues fitting passengers and luggage into the vehicle, I raised my concerns with the lady serving me and was told this is the only vehicle they have. Okay, great, well I paid for a larger vehicle - the lady was extremely rude, and unhelpful and proceeded to insult me in Spanish (what they didn’t know is I had google translate open on my phone)
I was so fed up at this point, had two restless young children so had to try and make the best of a bad situation, therefore I accepted the vehicle and proceeded to load my luggage and get my children into the vehicle. Upon inspection there was considerable damage to the front number that was not recorded on the document I had signed so photographed this and returned to the office - they advised they would document this (I do not hold out any hope - p!ss up in a brewery came to mind)
Again I went to leave wanting to just get on my journey, extremely frustrated, it was at this point I started the vehicle and there was only 60km of fuel left and a low tyre pressure warning, despite the document I signed stating it was full to full (meaning I’d have to return the vehicle full of fuel) - so again, I returned to the office advised of this situation and was told I could either wait for it to be filled with fuel or just return it with the same amount of fuel. Lacking confidence in the whole management system I opted for them to fill the vehicle to which they were again rude and ultimately throwing there weight around as if I had done something wrong. So unload the luggage, get the kids out the car, wait half an hour and finally get the vehicle back. Some what 3 hours later I was finally on my way, still with tyre pressure issues but I just wanted to get the hell out of there. I will never ever use Avis Budget again, anywhere in my travels and I would advise anybody else to pay that little bit more and go elsewhere. AVOID AVIS BUDGET LIKE THE PLAGUE. The company and there operation in Girona is not fit for purpose and should be closed down!

Really disappointing, especially given the reviews and how packed the place was. The setting is great and the huge wood-fired grill looks fantastic, but unfortunately the food didn't live up to it.
We shared the grilled vegetables, entrecôte, lamb chops and veal. Nothing seemed to be seasoned. The vegetables were bland until we added salt and red wine vinegar ourselves. The entrecôte was tough, the lamb chops were tiny and didn't really taste of lamb, and overall the three meats somehow just tasted like generic grilled meat. Even the aioli tasted more like mayonnaise than aioli.
In retrospect I should have taken the hint when the waiter suggested peppercorn sauce with the meat.
They bring you a plate with olives, raw garlic, whole tomatoes. Then they charge you for it at the end. What a ripoff.
At the end I just heard Gordon Ramsay's voice saying, What a shame.
The best thing I had all evening was the complimentary shot at the end.

If you enjoy flavor, go somewhere else.

Today I went to pick up an order for €35. When she showed me the bacon, the clerk opened the box very quickly and I was the one who noticed that one was broken. When I asked her if she could change it, she said no. After waiting for some solution, she finally offered to discount the amount and the total was €33.

After paying, when I was leaving, I noticed that on the door they indicated that the pastry shop applied a discount with the Carnet Jove. I asked her if they did and she replied that they did, but that since I had already paid, she could not rectify the charge. She had not asked me before if I had the card or informed me of this discount. The only answer was that she would apply it to me “next time”.

The problem is not only the money, but the feeling of little attention and lack of interest in finding solutions: if I don't detect the broken bacon, I take it away; and if I don't see the Carnet Jove badge when I leave, I don't find out about the discount either.

With the prices and the name of this bakery, I expected much more careful and professional attention. After this experience, there will be no next time.

one_star_reviews.text:
DO NOT BOOK WITH THIS AGENCY.

Based on our experience, getting our €3,200 deposit back was an unacceptable ordeal. Our tenancy ended on 1 July 2026, and our contract stated that the deposit would be returned within seven days. Instead, we had to chase My Space Barcelona for almost two months.

We were repeatedly given excuses: the person responsible was supposedly out of the office, then on her lunch break. Promised call-backs never happened, and even arranged call-back appointments were missed because she was suddenly unavailable again. We were continuously strung along with promises that the money would be transferred, but nothing happened.

A few weeks after moving out, I happened to be back in Barcelona and went to their office in person. I was once again assured that the deposit would be paid by the following Monday. After that, they stopped responding again.

We only received the full deposit on 1 September 2026 after involving our lawyers and putting further pressure on the company. One of their own employees even advised us to involve lawyers because the manager had stopped responding to them.

I actually used to recommend this agency, which makes this experience even more disappointing. This was not a simple delay or misunderstanding. We were repeatedly given excuses and empty promises, and were genuinely worried that we might never get our money back.

Afterwards, I found several other public reviews describing similar problems with deposits and communication. Based on our experience, I strongly advise against booking with My Space Barcelona. Getting your own deposit back should not require legal pressure, a personal visit to their office and weeks of chasing.

one_star_reviews.text:
On August 12th, 2026, I visited Les Moles with a friend for their solar eclipse viewing event. The €175-per-person experience included a special menu and live orchestra, which seemed fair for a one-Michelin-star tasting menu. We arrived around 6:45 p.m. for the pre-eclipse portion. We were not greeted and had very little interaction with staff throughout the evening, though our interactions were friendly.

We found the other guests gathered in a shaded area beside the outdoor dining tables. I was surprised by the number of tables—roughly 80–90—given the quality of food associated with the price. I was impressed by their ambition, especially with approximately 238 guests attending. The heat was intense, but wine, beer, and soda were provided while we waited. Small bites were also served. The first was a cold fish salad that lacked salt and reminded me of canned tuna. Three flavorful croquettes followed and were much better. However, it was clear that the restaurant was overwhelmed. The orchestra spent much of this time doing a sound check, rather than providing music, which made the opening feel poorly organized.

The eclipse itself was undoubtedly the highlight. We walked up the hill around 8:00 p.m., where wine and cushions were provided. The viewing was well executed, although I found the orchestra underutilized. Music was only briefly played after totality; playing it beforehand could have added to the anticipation.

We returned to our tables around 9:00 p.m. and were excited to find ourselves near the stage. Unfortunately, the stage remained empty for the entire dinner, and there was no music. Our table was crowded with utensils and three wine glasses per person, one of which remained unused. After waiting roughly 20 minutes, we received the beet tartare with tomato and almond. It was beautiful and easily the best dish of the night, with excellent balance and an incredible sauce. Unfortunately, our empty plates remained for more than 20 minutes, and the next course arrived before they were cleared.

The black-and-white garlic sauce was confusingly presented beside the dirty plate, making us think it was a side dish. It was an okay bite, but without the bread it lacked much excitement, and the bread took another 10 minutes to arrive after we asked twice. After another 20-minute wait came vermouth jelly with foie gras and brioche. It was similarly underwhelming, though the brioche provided good texture.

The langoustine was perfectly cooked but almost flavorless, with a bland sauce that dominated the dish. The veal cheek was even worse: the sauces were one-dimensional, while the meat was dry and flavorless, making it easily my least favorite veal cheek I have ever eaten. Many plates being cleared still had food on them. Dessert was a chocolate dish with several components. It was pleasant, but nothing particularly memorable.

The orchestra performed after we left. Other reviews have praised it, but by then we had spent more than three hours at the table and had no desire to stay. Throughout dinner, I also asked servers about the dishes, but none could provide information beyond what was written on the menu. At a Michelin-starred restaurant, I believe guests should be able to learn about the ideas and stories behind each dish.

Ultimately, the food was nowhere near Michelin-star quality and would have been disappointing even at €40. The service was clearly overwhelmed by the number of guests, making the event feel as though scale and revenue had been prioritized over the quality of the experience. Despite this, I still think we enjoyed ourselves more than many other guests, who often appeared bored or disengaged.

That said, I believe this was likely an unusual one-off event rather than a reflection of Les Moles as a whole. Their regular menu is highly praised, and I admire the ambition behind attempting an event of this scale. I also appreciated the effort and friendliness of some of the servers. I hope to see what Les Moles can accomplish under more normal circumstances.

On Friday, August 28, 2026, we were waiting for the 4:15 PM bus from Cruces to Castro.

When it didn't arrive, I asked the driver who was supposed to come at 4:50 PM from the surrounding villages at that stop, and he told me it was because it was a holiday due to the Bilbao festivities. What does the Cruces-Castro line have to do with Bilbao to be considered a holiday? Nowhere was the time change announced; there was no information sheet on the buses, nor was it posted on the company's website in the days leading up to the announcement.
Since we couldn't go to Bilbao to catch the bus because of the time, we had to wait for the 5:30 PM bus from Cruces, as it was supposedly a holiday, later than usual.
When the bus arrived, I asked the driver why that service was listed as a holiday and tried to explain what the previous driver had told me.
He started raising his voice, yelling at me and not letting me explain. I raised my voice as well, and he threatened to kick me off the bus if I didn't sit down. I spoke to him respectfully at all times, until I couldn't take his arrogance, shouting, and threats to kick me out any longer.

This is what happens with most drivers; we passengers have to keep quiet and put up with their disrespect, their bad attitudes, and their bad moods.

The bus is late and doesn't keep to the schedule. The driver on the Bilbao-Castro route and vice versa is incredibly rude; I don't know how he can still work with the public. He argues with at least two or three passengers per trip; he's unbearable. Some people have even refused to ride with him and waited for the next bus just to avoid dealing with him. He's a very rude man, around 50 years old. I'm also considering not riding with him again if he's still on the bus.

At the next table there were people eating who were also absolutely shocked at how we were treated in the restaurant. Remove the dog friendly tag from your website. You can't expect much from a restaurant that looks like a garage from the outside, and we gave it a chance for no reason. You are the only restaurant of this standard where the dog's place is indicated by signs on the dirty floors. This experience made the quality restaurants in the Costa del Sol area even more valuable, where our dog was extremely welcome and always got to sit in his own basket on his own chair.

Good luck!

one_star_reviews.text:
I Unfortunately, I had a really bad experience tonight and, with regret, I’m leaving 1 star.

Starting with the positives, the venue itself is very nice, aesthetic, stylish and has a great atmosphere visually. “Luxurious,” though? I personally wouldn’t go that far. It felt similar to many beach clubs you can find around Marbella or other Mediterranean seaside destinations.

The entrance was quite expensive at €70 per person. If you see many positive reviews from women, is because they are asking from girls to leave a five star review so they can get inside for free!!!

Later in the evening, we went to the back area of the club and, when we tried to come back inside, there was a queue. We waited patiently for over 10 minutes. When we reached the front, several other people were allowed in ahead of us. I eventually asked, “Excuse me, what about us?” The woman at the door laughed and responded sarcastically, “Do you have VIP? No. They have priority. You need this (showing me her lanyard) to be VIP. You don’t have that!”

I genuinely didn’t know that was the system, so I simply said, “Oh okay, sorry, I didn’t know.” She then looked at her colleague and they both laughed. It was unnecessarily rude and made us feel quite uncomfortable.

Unfortunately, that wasn’t the worst part. Later, a waiter was walking through the crowd carrying a large ice bucket/box with bottles of Belvedere inside. As he passed me, he hit me quite hard on the head with it. It was painful and left me feeling dizzy. I looked at him and asked what he was doing, especially as he hadn’t even apologised. He simply looked at me and walked away.

For reference, a basic spirit with a soft drink was around €20. Crazy expensive for no reason.

I genuinely tried to enjoy the night. We stayed for more than five hours, listened to the music and tried to make the most of it, but unfortunately almost every interaction I had with the staff left a bad impression.

For a venue charging these kinds of prices, basic courtesy and customer service should not depend on whether somebody has a VIP table or a standard entrance ticket. Whether someone spends €70 at the door or hundreds of euros on a table, they are still a paying customer and deserve to be treated with respect.

Beautiful venue, but based on the way we were treated, I unfortunately wouldn’t return.

one_star_reviews.text:
If you don't want to feel like a product, just another number in a chain, this probably isn't the place for you.

A deeply disappointing experience. If you still have time, don't get your treatments here.

We underwent treatment with an external gynecologist who used the clinic's facilities. Before the transfer, that doctor made sure to perform all the necessary tests and didn't proceed with the transfer until he was certain everything was in order. Unfortunately, that pregnancy didn't continue.

We decided to resume the process, but this time with the clinic's own medical team. And that's when our nightmare began. What the hell was the point?

I felt like I stopped being a patient and became just a number and a sum of money. We went in for a transfer without the gynecologist having performed practically any prior checks. No transfer test was performed to assess whether everything was correct, nor was it properly verified that my uterus was in optimal condition for implantation. This is something we consider fundamental, based on our previous experience and what we have subsequently discovered. They gave me a date and said, "See you then," without any follow-up whatsoever. I only had one blood test because I requested it; I had made a mistake with my medication one day and was afraid it might affect the process.

The result, of course, was that the transfer was unsuccessful. Why were our embryos used without thoroughly verifying beforehand that everything was prepared to attempt implantation? Pure business. A gynecologist at that clinic once told us, "As a business, it's in my best interest for you to use up your eggs so you have to have more retrieved." The other one only said it... this one actually did it.

Regarding the staff, I want to emphasize that Marina and the nurse Cristina were, by far, the professionals who made us feel most supported and treated us with humanity.

On the contrary, if you have to be seen by nurse Andrea, I'm sorry to say! It was a terrible experience from the moment we arrived at the clinic. She made it clear that since we were being treated by an external gynecologist, we weren't their patients (but of course, the fee is exactly the same as if you were doing everything with them; you sign the consent forms with them...). She is an extremely cold, distant, and judgmental person, which I consider especially inappropriate in such a vulnerable process. For us, it was undoubtedly one of the worst experiences at the clinic, and we had to request that she be removed from our case.

The second gynecologist who saw us also fell short of what we expected from a clinic specializing in assisted reproduction. The overall feeling was one of a lack of follow-up, tests, and, above all, a lack of compassion.

I want to issue a particularly important warning: don't be swayed solely by the fact that it's a well-known chain or by the clinic's reputation and references. Investigate, ask questions, demand explanations, and above all, make sure they are performing the necessary tests before using your embryos.

With everything that has happened, and despite it meaning starting over, both financially and emotionally, we were forced to change clinics, and after only two appointments, we left both in tears. But this time it was for the complete opposite reason: because of the human touch, the professionalism and dedication, the time they gave us, the tests they requested and performed, and the NEW DIAGNOSIS they presented us with. We cried again, this time out of anger and helplessness. Because now we're left with the feeling that we wasted our embryos when perhaps the conditions weren't right for attempting implantation.

If you're going through a similar process, my advice is not to do it here. Go where you truly feel you're being treated like a person and not just a number.

An experience I honestly wouldn't wish on anyone.

one_star_reviews.text:
⭐ Very bad experience. We wouldn't go back.

We arrived at 4:00 PM, which is supposedly when they open, and were told we'd have to wait. Meanwhile, the staff calmly started making their coffees. We ordered one ourselves and were told they couldn't serve us yet. They said it would be about 15 minutes, but we ended up waiting half an hour before they decided to start serving.

From then on, it was all surprises. Non-slip socks are mandatory, but they don't allow you to use your own, even if they're perfectly fine: you have to buy the ones from the establishment. Furthermore, if you have a small child and need to go in to accompany them, you also have to buy and pay for your own socks.

Something similar happened with the price. Their own instructions state that an hour costs €9 on weekdays and €10 on weekends. We came on a Tuesday and they charged us €10, claiming that they apply that price until school starts. A condition that, at least in the information we saw, wasn't mentioned.

They also advertise that an additional hour costs €6. When we tried to pay for it, they told us we couldn't because there were too many people and they didn't allow extending the time. We completely understand that there might be a capacity limit, but then they should clearly inform customers of this possibility before entering, especially if they explicitly advertise the option to pay for additional hours.

But the worst part, honestly, was the staff's attitude. In particular, the woman who served us was extremely unfriendly and unkind from the start. When you go with a child to have a pleasant time, the least you expect is decent service.

Between opening half an hour later than advertised, the prices and conditions that don't match the information displayed, the mandatory additional charges, and the treatment we received, our experience was very negative. It's a shame, because the concept of the place could be very good, but the service and management leave much to be desired.

From the beginning, the experience was frustrating. Finding the pickup point from the airport was extremely difficult due to unclear instructions, and we ultimately had to pay €22 for a taxi to get there.

When we arrived, the office was packed and clearly understaffed, with only two customer service employees handling customers. We were then told to wait while they “cleaned” the car, which resulted in a wait of more than 30 minutes.

The condition of the facility was also disappointing. The walls were dirty, chairs were loose or broken, and the ceiling was leaking directly above the customer service counter. A bucket had been placed underneath to collect the water, right where customers were standing.

Unfortunately, the return process was just as problematic. There were around 10 cars waiting and only one staff member handling everything. When we asked about the shuttle to the airport, we were told it came every 10–15 minutes. However, we ended up waiting more than 40 minutes. When we raised the issue with a staff member, she became confrontational and started yelling, telling us that it was a “courtesy bus” and that they were not obligated to take us. Unfortunately, she was not wearing a name tag, so I was unable to get her name.

At that point, we were genuinely worried about missing our flight. After seeing several other customers who had also been waiting give up and order taxis, we did the same.

The prices may be competitive, but in my opinion, they do not make up for this level of service. This is also the only rental company we encountered that did not have an office inside the airport, which made the whole process even more inconvenient.

It’s disappointing to see a company operating such a poorly maintained and understaffed facility, combined with such unprofessional customer service. I hope management takes this feedback seriously, because there is significant room for improvement.

⭐ 1/5

Absolutely appalling customer service.

I ordered a wooden pizza peel from García de Pou and it arrived damaged. I reported the issue immediately and provided the necessary information. Instead of simply taking responsibility for a damaged product delivered to their customer, García de Pou tried to hide behind their carrier, GLS.

That is not my problem. My purchase was made with García de Pou, not with GLS.

What followed is even worse. Despite several emails and repeated attempts to get this resolved, they have now simply stopped responding altogether. No solution, no refund, no proper follow-up — just silence.

That is not merely poor customer service. It is disrespectful and completely unacceptable.

A damaged delivery can happen to any company. What matters is how a company handles it afterwards. García de Pou has shown exactly how not to do it: shifting responsibility, failing to resolve the issue, ignoring the customer and ultimately refusing to communicate at all.

I have now had to formally demand termination of the purchase and a refund. I no longer want a replacement product from this company. I simply want my money back and to close this matter.

For a company of this size, this level of customer service is frankly embarrassing.

Based on my experience, I would strongly advise others to think twice before ordering from García de Pou. If something goes wrong with your order, you may find yourself chasing them for a solution — until they simply stop responding.

one_star_reviews.text:
If I could give zero stars, I would.

I previously had a pleasant experience using MiFibra for my phone and internet while I lived in Spain. I terminated my contract when I left the country in 2022.

To my surprise, almost four years later, I suddenly began receiving emails claiming that I had two outstanding bills to pay. These emails included threats of legal proceedings, asset seizure, and being placed on debt registers.

The emails initially went to my spam folder, which is hardly surprising. MiFibra was an internet and telephone provider I had not used for approximately four years, so I had no reason to expect legitimate correspondence from them. I only discovered the messages when I checked the folder.

I contacted their customer service through WhatsApp, explained that something was clearly wrong, and asked them to identify exactly what they claimed I had not paid.

Their representative then told me that it was actually one unpaid bill from the termination of my contract in August 2022. This already contradicted their collection emails, which referred to two bills.

When I explained that I had never received any notification about an unpaid August 2022 bill, they claimed that they had contacted me previously. Immediately afterwards, I received another email presenting an old message from October 2021 as supposed proof.

That October 2021 email concerned a late payment from almost a year before the termination of my contract and was for a completely different amount. It obviously did not prove the existence of an unpaid final bill from August 2022. It only created another contradiction in an already incoherent story.

Their different communications referred to different numbers of bills, different dates, different circumstances, and different amounts. None of it matched.

I then formally disputed the alleged debt by both email and WhatsApp and asked them to provide clear documentary evidence identifying exactly what they were claiming. Since then, they have gone completely silent.

I strongly recommend that anyone receiving a payment demand from this company check every detail carefully and insist on complete documentation before paying anything.

A company that sends threatening legal notices to a former customer almost four years after a contract ended, cannot consistently identify the debt it claims is owed, produces irrelevant correspondence as supposed proof, and then stops responding when formally challenged is not a company I believe can be trusted.

Completely unacceptable and deeply unprofessional.

one_star_reviews.text:
Disappointing and unprofessional. We paid a 50% deposit for the manufacture of a bar for our establishment, and when we requested a refund, they deducted €396 + VAT for "services rendered," even though no work had actually been done to justify that amount. We even provided them with the necessary measurements and photographs.

When we signed the contract, we were assured that the bar would be ready by mid-September, within the stated 45-day timeframe. However, just a few days after paying the deposit, they informed us that it would finally be ready by the end of October, now citing the August closure as the reason—something that wasn't explained to us in that way before we signed the contract.

All of this has caused us to lose time, money, and revenue, in addition to delaying our project. We understand that unforeseen circumstances can arise, but we don't think it's fair that we have to bear the consequences of information that, from our point of view, wasn't clear from the beginning. We expected much more professionalism and transparency.

one_star_reviews.text:
Terrible experience at this bar.

It was our first time in Gran Canaria and had thus far had a fantastic experience, myself and my friends came into this bar and ordered drinks and danced, around 10 minutes later I needed the bathroom so left my drink on the bar at the corner closest to the toilets, the bar staff saw me do this then head to the toilet. When I came back no later than 5 minutes later to retrieve my drink it was gone and one member of the bar staff was stood laughing at me. I approached him and asked where my drink had gone, he continued to laugh and say he didnt know what I was talking about? I explained I went to the toilet, came back and the bar had been cleaned and my drink was gone, the member of bar staff then flew into a rage shouting and saying I was accusing him of stealing.. the situation got completely out of control and I was visibly upset,  the bar man then told me he would call security/the police, a complete overreaction, I was not aggressive whatsoever. another lovely member of staff a lady could see that I was being honest so offered to replace my drink, the barman I had initially dealt with saw this and told her to not give me another under any circumstances. She winked at me and I could tell once the bar man had backed off she would replace my drink which I really appreciated. When she replaced my drink though she demanded payment, at this point I just cut my losses and paid. Of course I understand if there is some form of policy prohibiting leaving drinks on the bar but the bar staff had the opportunity to tell me this multiple times if this had been the case? Instead they denied any and all knowledge.

Some of the customers in bar were also extremely hostile towards me because I was English, grabbing members of staff and asking them why we were sitting near to them in Spanish, I even asked a member of the Spanish group whether there friend was talking about us and he confirmed she was.. the unnecessary hostility made absolutely no sense to me.

Lastly when the bar closed and we were sat outside on the steps outside we were approached by 4 Middle Eastern lads asking if we wanted to buy drugs, we declined and they began to laugh at us and talk about us individually in their own language. I asked what they were laughing at (by this point I was tired of the hostility I had recieved all night) and things began to get heated, I decided to leave based on better judgement, being abroad in a foreign country. The 4 men then followed me chasing me back to my hotel.

Safe to say I will absolutely not be returning to this bar. It’s a shame and definitely put somewhat of a dampener on our holiday.

Be careful with the guys on the stairs offering drugs; they're professional thieves and criminals. Every time we walk past there, we're scared. As for the club, it's a good place to go out and all, but those criminals and the fact that they don't do anything about it is damaging the place and the tourist area.

I want to emphasize that this isn't the first time I've experienced what you see in the photos at this establishment: rusty and worn-out pans, dirty dishes, and so on.

Best regards to the owner of this business. I'm leaving indefinitely, hoping that things improve and that guests start respecting themselves, as I believe this is a place worth visiting.

one_star_reviews.text: The service is awful 😡 We religiously pay for maintenance every month, and it leaves much to be desired. We have a 24/7/365 service contract. On Friday, August 7, 2026, the elevator broke down on the 6th floor of the 7-story building. They notified us, but the technician didn't show up until Saturday 🤬🤬. We've been told so many lies that we don't know what to believe anymore. The result is 12 days in a beach building, with two people on the 6th floor who can only enjoy the 15 days their children are allowed to bring them and stay with them, as both are over 90 years old. We're on the 5th floor; my husband is diabetic with frequent drops in blood sugar and other chronic illnesses, and I have lumbosacral radiculopathy, spinal curvature, and various other aches and pains. Our next-door neighbors bring their parents to enjoy the building, as they are also over 85. On the 4th floor, there's a 96-year-old neighbor suffering from depression due to the loss of his wife. He has a pacemaker, circulatory problems, and other health issues. He uses a walker and therefore can't leave his house. He's begging his daughter to let him go home. I don't think this is right. We're trapped in our homes because we can't go downstairs, let alone upstairs, and I'm the youngest in the group. Now the technician has come with the famous part that supposedly Seur lost last week and had to reorder. I don't believe a word of it. Now they can't get the part out, or some other story. The result is that the part has to be taken to the workshop in Jerez to be retrieved. 🤦🏻‍♀️🤦🏻‍♀️ So we don't know tomorrow if they'll fix it or not. I believe this should be reported to consumer protection agencies and the industry authorities. If we have a service contract, and the elevator is supposedly old, why are they responsible for its maintenance and don't have spare parts? I hope the building manager demands a refund for the days the elevator is out of service. Furthermore, this isn't the first time this has happened. If I remember correctly, they had us out of service for at least 10 days before because of a plastic pulley, but the neighbors weren't affected. Since it's a building in Chipiona, and most of the owners are elderly and only come in occasionally, it directly impacts us residents. Seeing all the negative comments, the company should take action. During the lockdown, even though we couldn't leave our homes, the elevator was working, and we could go up to the terrace for a walk and some fresh air or down to the parking garage. It was just the elderly couple across the street and us, with my mother, who has reduced mobility and whom we had to take out to the garage in her wheelchair so she wouldn't get overwhelmed. For me, it's like being held captive in my own home. I have to thank some of my neighbors for their help, because even my neighbor's sister, who was here on vacation, came every day to take out the trash and bring me food if I needed it, because they knew about my husband's diabetes and that he can't eat junk food. Other neighbors have had to go to the pharmacy for his medication, like blood sugar test strips, blood pressure pills, and so on. I had to place an order with Mercadona online with the help of a relative who lived 150 km away. He told me not to worry about having to carry the food up the stairs because he had a device that helps the delivery cart. I apologized to the delivery guy for having to carry it up the stairs 🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻 I felt so sorry for him. I wanted to give him a tip for being so kind and understanding because he helped me by putting everything on the counter so I wouldn't have to bend down and lift it. I wanted to give him a tip, but he wouldn't accept it. He said it was against company policy. I felt even more sorry for him because of the heat and the effort he was making. 🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻 I hope they fix it tomorrow because even if I can't go to the beach, at least I can get bread, go to the pharmacy, and buy the fruits and vegetables we need. Thank you to my neighbors for their help; may God bless them with good health.

one_star_reviews.text:
De las fotos a la realidad hay bastante diferencia. Lo que esperas encontrar por las imágenes no se corresponde con lo que finalmente te encuentras.

La limpieza deja bastante que desear: la cama, sin funda de colchón, resulta poco higiénica. Además, durante nuestra estancia no tuvimos agua caliente en la ducha y el papel higiénico era bastante escaso. La recepción estaba cerrada y no había prácticamente nadie a quien poder pedir ayuda o solucionar cualquier incidencia.

El mantenimiento general también es claramente mejorable: piscina con el agua verdosa, césped bastante quemado, elementos muy oxidados y un ascensor que no funciona, aunque se indica que el acceso a las plantas superiores debe hacerse por las escaleras.

Lo único positivo del acceso a la playa es precisamente su dificultad, porque hace que esa zona esté bastante menos masificada.

Y mención aparte para el equipo del chiringuito Pez Melón, que fue maravilloso y nos atendió fenomenal.

In short: a location with potential, but the state of the facilities, the cleanliness and the lack of attention make the experience quite far from what the photographs show.

Small portions, terrible service, and an extremely disrespectful “chef” (see attached picture).

And the cherry on the cake? The insults from the “chef” himself.

There really isn’t much more to say. This place clearly only cares about making a profit, not about the people they are serving, and the ridiculous portion sizes are a perfect example of that.

It is truly disappointing to see a restaurant treat its customers with such little respect, especially when we have been regular customers. Hospitality should be about treating people with basic respect and providing a decent experience, not simply maximizing profit at the customer’s expense.

Es Vivers, you should be ashamed of the way you treat your customers. We certainly won’t ever be coming back.
